text:
alice: Heads-up, vuln scan flagged three issues impacting our Go services: grpc (remote DoS), github.com/golang-jwt/jwt (signature validation edge case), and a net/http handler path traversal concern. Can we triage?
sec-bot: Automated scan results: 
- CVE-2025-2101 (google.golang.org/grpc) - medium, requires backportable fix v1.56.1+
- CVE-2025-1987 (github.com/golang-jwt/jwt) - high, patch available v4.4.3
- CVE-2025-1770 (stdlib net/http usage pattern) - low/medium, mitigations suggested
Link: https://scanner.internal/reports/1763500000
ryan: Thanks. Which services use the vulnerable grpc surface?
maya: api-gateway, model-proxy, and internal-catalog. api-gateway is highest risk because it's internet-facing.
dan: jwt lib used in auth-service and session-worker. We do token verification in a couple places with custom validation; need to audit usage.
carol: net/http issue occurs when using filepath.Clean with user-supplied path in file server. I posted a quick grep result: `grep -R "ServeFile(" ./services | wc -l` -> 3 hits.
alice: Initial plan: create a single PR per repo to bump deps (no replace hacks), run unit + integration, then canary deploy to dedicated pool. Agree?
ryan: Yes. For grpc, target upstream recommended version: `google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.1` (or whatever scanner suggests). For jwt: `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v4.4.3`. For net/http, prefer code fix + add tests.
maya: I'll open PRs for auth-service and api-gateway. Dan, can you handle session-worker and model-proxy?
dan: On it. Also checking if any pinned versions in monorepo break semver.
carol: For the file server cases I can submit a small patch to validate path prefixes and add tests. Example patch snippet: ```go
// prevent path traversal
p := filepath.Clean("/" + req.URL.Path)
if !strings.HasPrefix(p, "/static/") {
    http.Error(w, "not found", http.StatusNotFound)
    return
}
```
ops-lead: Rollout plan: canary 5% on dedicated, 30m burn, ramp to 25% then 100% if no errors. Add alert: 5xx spike > 2x baseline or jwt verification errors > 0.1% should rollback.
alice: We should also pin CI Docker images and the Go toolchain to avoid transient builds. Recommend go1.21.3-builder image.
ryan: Question: do we need emergency rotation of any KMS keys because of jwt issue? I think not — it's a validation bug, not key leak. But we should audit all signing keys usage.
maya: Agree. I'll add a KMS key usage report job to run once (list keys used by auth-service).
carol: Also add audit logging for token verification failures (redact PII). We currently log only success/fail counts; add stack traces to debug-level only.
dan: For PRs, include go.mod diffs like: ```diff
- github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.4.1
+ github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.4.3
- google.golang.org/grpc v1.55.0
+ google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.1
```
alice: Good. Label PRs with `security/urgent` and tag oncall. I'll draft a blameless postmortem template in case of issues.ops-lead: Make sure console observability (Redwood Console) has token-level traces enabled for canary windows. Keep cost low by sampling 1% but keep full error traces.
ryan: Any vendor-managed services using older go versions? We should scan build logs; some internal functions still use go1.18 in CI. That needs upgrade tickets.
maya: Created auth-service PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/412 (bump jwt + tests). Added unit tests for the validation edge case.
dan: Created model-proxy PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-proxy/pull/219 (bump grpc). Running CI.
carol: Opened small patch for file server: https://git.internal/redwood/web-static/pull/33 — includes new test vectors.
sec-bot: CVE tracker updated: all three issues marked "in-progress" and assigned to participants.
alice: Next steps: finish PR reviews today, merge after green CI, canary tonight at 22:00 UTC. Notify #incidents if rollout hits thresholds.
ryan: I'll prepare a rollback plan (revert PRs + re-deploy previous images).
maya: Also adding a short smoke test that hits token verification edge case and a healthcheck for grpc open streams.
carol: Don't forget to update dependency docs and CHANGELOG entries (security subsection).
dan: One gotcha: some internal packages import `jwt` through a forked path — searching for `golang-jwt` only missed it. I ran `rg "github.com/.*/jwt"` and found two forks. I'll patch those imports.
alice: Perfect. If anything escalates, page sec-oncall. Otherwise I'll close this thread after the canary completes. :thumbsup:
